claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about your son Alex who is 6 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions:

**Is Alex living with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand more about the situation.

**Are you contributing towards Alex's upkeep? For example, do you provide regular financial support or payments for his care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his clothes, food, and other things he needs regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know you're contributing financially to Alex's upkeep.

Now I need to ask: **Who does Alex currently live with?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one more important question:

**Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not living in the UK at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one final question:

**Which country are you currently living in, and are you still considered ordinarily resident in the UK (meaning you normally live in the UK but are temporarily abroad)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad now, and no, I wouldn't say I'm ordinarily resident in the UK anymore. I've moved away.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

To claim Child Benefit, you must meet the UK residence requirements. Child Benefit is generally only available to people who are living in the UK or are ordinarily resident in the UK. Since you're living abroad and are no longer ordinarily resident in the UK, you don't meet this fundamental requirement.

While it's positive that you contribute financially to Alex's upkeep (with clothes, food, and other necessities), and his mother isn't currently claiming Child Benefit for him, the residence requirement must be met first before any other factors can be considered.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you return to live in the UK - you would be able to apply for Child Benefit at that time, provided you meet all the other eligibility criteria.
